content: The efficacy of tetracyclines may be reduced when co-administered with calcium carbonate. To avoid this interaction, administer tetracyclines separately from calcium carbonate-containing products. Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of intravenous sodium phosphates by binding cations in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored in such cases. Calcium decreases serum phosphate levels by binding dietary phosphate. Alternative treatments should be considered if available. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride increase the toxicity of calcium carbonate through mechanisms related to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. This combination may elevate the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. Calcium carbonate reduces the solubility and bioavailability of velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH, which can significantly impair its efficacy. Velpatasvir is practically insoluble at a pH greater than 5. To mitigate this, administer velpatasvir at least 4 hours apart from antacids. Calcium carbonate decreases the absorption and efficacy of sotalol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH, which may lower its bioavailability and efficacy. Administer sparsentan 2 hours before or after antacids to minimize this interaction. Calcium carbonate increases the toxicity of squill through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Calcium carbonate reduces the absorption of strontium ranelate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. Calcium carbonate decreases the absorption of tiludronate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 30 minutes. Calcium carbonate reduces the absorption of timolol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of trandolapril through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of ursodiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Calcium carbonate decreases the absorption of vadadustat by binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer vadadustat at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after calcium carbonate to minimize this interaction. Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of verapamil through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Calcium carbonate reduces the solubility and bioavailability of vismodegib by increasing gastric pH, which may alter its efficacy. Use caution and monitor closely. The concurrent use of vitamin D with calcium salts is generally beneficial but may lead to hypercalcemia in some patients. Monitor calcium levels closely.
